note: The site is the High Street Roman road, a line some 20 km long between Brougham and Ambleside; the stored point is the fell summit, which the road crosses at its highest point (828 m, per the Lake District National Park Authority). The sources that give a point for the road itself disagree along its course: the Megalithic Portal gives 54.481105 N, 2.873988 W (about 1.35 km south of the stored point) and the Wikidata item of the scheduled section gives 54.5423 N, 2.84141 W in Bampton parish (about 5.8 km north); no two independent sources give the same point, so it is held for the owner.

The site named here is the whole Kola Peninsula (about 100,000 km2); Wikipedia puts its point at 67.688, 35.944 and Wikidata at 68.0, 36.0 (both one source family, 80-100 km from the stored point, which lies in the empty interior of Lovozersky district), and no independent source quotes a single point for the peninsula within 1 km of either, so the point is held for the owner.

The monument is a rock relief with an inscription about 100 m from the Fasıllar Hittite monument (Kültür Portalı). Only Vici.org prints a point for it (geo:37.65897,31.896641, about 0.67 km WNW of the stored point, which seems to sit in Fasıllar village); other pages give the Hittite monument's point, not this site's, so no two independent sources can be quoted and the point is held for the owner.

The only published point for Huankarán is the one on Wikidata/Spanish Wikipedia (-9.382, -76.707), a single source family; the MINCETUR tourism record (mirrored by turismoperuano.com) gives no coordinates and the site is not in OpenStreetMap, so no second independent source for the point can be quoted.

The site is Blennerhasset Roman fort (scheduled monument 1019017), which roman-britain.co.uk places at NY 190413 and the fort's own Wikidata item (Q17664654) at 54°45'36.720"N, 3°15'36.900"W (about 54.7602, -3.2603), roughly 1.15 km north-west of the stored parish point; only the Wikimedia family prints decimal/DMS coordinates for the fort in readable form (Historic England and ancientmonuments.uk refuse automated requests), so no second independent source can be quoted and the point is held for the owner.

The Finnish Heritage Agency register (kyppi.fi, Mankby (Mankki) 1000001861) places the deserted village site 4.5 km south-west of Espoo church at Lat 60.19219541, Lon 24.57913599; the stored point is Espoo church itself, about 4.5 km off. The only other point found, Wikidata's P625 (60.192193, 24.579144), is a copy of the register value, and no independent source (OpenStreetMap has no feature) prints the site's coordinates, so the point is held for the owner with the register value as the lead.

The site is only 'a Bronze Age burial mound' at Gårdstånga (English Wikipedia; its photo 'Bronsåldershög vid Gårdstånga' carries no location), and the parish holds more than a dozen registered mounds (Utshög 4:1, Killehög 5:1, Gårdstånga 19:1, 28:1-48:1); the stored point is Wikipedia's coarse 55°46′N 13°21′E for the village, and no source ties this site to one mound's point.

Only Wikidata prints a point for Gazma Cave (39.5383, 45.1793, about 3 km NNE of Tananam at about 1420 m). Wikipedia and the Imrani cave inventory put the cave 3 km north-east of Tananam, but the excavators' 2023 paper and kaspi.az say 3 km south-east. The stored point sits 0.6 km from the village and 2.8 km from the Wikidata point. No second independent source with coordinates was found, so the point is held for the owner.

Batham Gate is a linear Roman road (Buxton to Brough-on-Noe, about 16 km); the stored point lies on its line near Peak Dale (English Wikipedia's point), while the Derbyshire HER centres the route at SK 13328 79159 (about 53.309, -1.801, which is Wikidata's point, 6.4 km away); no second independent source prints a latitude/longitude for either point, so it is held for the owner.

The site is the Early Bronze Age tell Maxta I (Maxta Kültəpəsi I) at Maxta village. Only the 2026 PLOS ONE study prints a point for it (39°35'23.61" N, 44°56'21.95" E, about 0.7 km west of the stored point). Wikipedia, Wikidata and GeoNames give only the village's coordinates, so no second independent source for the site's point exists and the point is held for the owner.

The site is the Roman villa at the locality Crkvine/Crkvina in the village of Bela Reka; Wikipedia and CHRE only give the village's point (CHRE says its point is 'Centred on village/city'), and no source prints a point for the villa itself.

The temple stood at Gerf Hussein about 90 km south of Aswan (Wikipedia/Wikidata 23.2833, 32.9, a whole-minute point, copied by the OSM node); most of its rock-cut part is submerged there, while its free-standing forecourt was reassembled at New Kalabsha, where the stored point lies and where the Megalithic Portal places it (23.960170, 32.867650). Each location has only one independent source family (Wikivoyage's New Kalabsha marker cannot be quoted as a coordinate pair, OSM has no feature there), so the point is held for the owner.

The Limes Germanicus is a frontier line of more than 550 km from the Rhine to the Danube, and its sources give arbitrary representative points for it (English Wikipedia 50.3, 7.8 near the Lahn; Wikidata 49.5, 9.5; GeoAtrium 49.796, 9.158 at Wörth am Main). No two independent sources give the same point, so the point is held for the owner.

Only Wikidata (34°45'34.675"N, 32°24'26.388"E) prints a point for the Asklepieion of Nea Paphos in a quotable form; the OpenStreetMap-derived Mapcarta page prints it only as mixed decimal/DMS values, and no heritage register, Pleiades or other independent page gives the sanctuary's point, so two independent sources cannot be quoted.

No page gives a point for a 'Casteddu di Puzzonu' in Sartène: the Wikipedia stubs (en, fr, co) and Wikidata carry no coordinates, and their only reference is a paper on a different site, Punta di Casteddu. The only excavated site named Puzzonu (ADLFI, Gallia) is a Bronze Age settlement in Quenza, not Sartène, so it cannot be taken as this site. The stored placeholder, shared with another site, is held for the owner.

site_name: Ex voto of the Arcadians, Delphi
note: No page gives a point for the Arcadian monument itself: Wikidata and the English and Greek Wikipedia articles carry no coordinates, and Arachne gives only the generic point of Delphi; the monument stands beside the Bull of the Corcyreans near the entrance of the sanctuary of Apollo, but no two independent sources can be quoted for its own point.

Only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family gives a point (-12.86125, -74.581472, 2.5 km SW of the stored point, which is Acobamba town itself); the MINCETUR inventory prints no coordinates and a tourism page places the caves 3.8 km north-east of Acobamba, so no two independent sources can be quoted for the site's point.

No two independent sources print a point for the site itself: Wikipedia and Wikidata give 16.90361, -89.44222, which on satellite imagery falls by a pond next to La Blanca village about 1 km south-west of the ruins, while the stored point matches the acropolis visible in its forest island and OpenStreetMap's La Blanca archaeological-site polygon (16.9107, -89.4360), a source whose page prints no quotable coordinate pair; GeoNames has no record of the site.

The stored point (16.317, -90.100, copied from English Wikipedia) is the namesake village Ucanal in Sayaxché, about 100 km from the ruins, and Wikidata's 16.86667, -89.35 lies some 2.5 km off; the site stands on the west bank of the Mopan near Pichelito II, where GeoNames records it at 16.84050, -89.36250 and the Ucanal Archaeological Project's 2018 report gives UTM N1864187.4, E248171.09 (zone 16, about 16.8475, -89.3634), but a UTM grid reference is not read and no second independent source prints a latitude/longitude for the site, so the point is held for the owner.

The location of Hedum is not established: English Wikipedia puts it in the town of Breza (44.019854, 18.264582), while Pleiades and the Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire (both from the Barrington Atlas, 'Podgora near Breza') place it at 43.990166, 18.290637, about 4 km away, and the Bosnian Wikipedia lists several competing locations. No two independent sources agree on one point.

The stored point is Cahal Pech's, about 4 km north of Chaa Creek. Only the Megalithic Portal gives a point for the Chaa Creek Maya site (17.110078 N, 89.074364 W); the other points found are the Lodge at Chaa Creek hotel (English Wikipedia, GeoNames) and the stream (Wikidata), not the ruins. Without a second independent source for the site itself, the point is held for the owner.

Only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family prints a point for Ayamachay (14°06′14″S 71°26′31″W, 1.2 km from the stored point); Hostnig's rupestreweb survey and Flores (2004) locate it only verbally (community of Orosqocha, left bank of the Salqa river, Combapata District), so no second independent source gives the site's point.

Wikipedia (en, az) places the Mərdangöl necropolis at Kharabagilan and the Ordubad society's page puts it near Sabirkənd and Kələntər-Dizə, about 17 km west of the stored point, which is Ordubad town. Only Wikidata prints a point for the necropolis itself (38.9483, 45.8436, 1.5 km east of those villages), so the stored point is wrong but no second independent source for the site's point was found; held for the owner.

No source prints a point for a Trypillia settlement at Kvitky: the only pages that mention one are copies of an English Wikipedia article deleted on 2026-01-29 (WP:CSD G12, its cited source did not mention the claim) and a Wikipedia list without coordinates, and the stored point (49.3136, 31.2341) lies at the village, which is not the site.

The only published points for the Treasury of the Boeotians are Wikidata's (38.481635, 22.501244) and the OpenStreetMap building outline shown by Mapcarta (38.48164, 22.50124), which are the same point and not demonstrably independent; English Wikipedia and Perseus give no coordinates, so no two independent sources can be quoted and the point is held for the owner.

Only Wikidata gives a point for Minanha (16.988, -89.075, 27.6 km north of the stored point); the English Wikipedia article prints no coordinates, XRONOS lists the site's coordinates as NA, and no other readable page gives the site's point, so it is held for the owner.

Wikipedia and Wikidata put Bülövqaya at 39.2834, 45.6382, about 2 km WSW of the stored point. The stored point is Göynük village itself; at about 1437 m, the Wikipedia point matches the site's published elevation of 1430-1452 m on the Sarısu river, the stored point does not. The excavation papers (TÜBA-AR, Amisos, AJAA) give no coordinates, so no second independent source for the site's point exists; held for the owner.

The stored point lies in Üçağız village (ancient Teimiussa) on the mainland, about 2.5 km from the sunken ruins on the north shore of Kekova Island; Wikipedia and Wikidata only give the island's centre (36.183, 29.883), and the ruins' point (about 36.1813, 29.8652 in Kulturenvanteri and OpenStreetMap) is not printed as text on two independent quotable pages, so the point is held for the owner.

Two places carry this name in Mersin: the castle at Çavuşlu, Tarsus (the linked Wikidata item, 37.1528, 34.9256, 33 km away) and the Kızlar Kalesi monastery in Toroslar near Çandır, which Mersin Metropolitan Municipality's VR page places at 36.9966-34.6108, about 0.9 km from the stored point - so the stored point is the Toroslar namesake, not the Wikidata castle. Only that one page prints a point for the Toroslar site, so no two independent sources can be quoted; held for the owner to settle which site the entry means.
